title: Hawaiian Airlines begins construction of premium Honolulu lounge as Alaska Airlines’ new Seattle lounge begins to take shape
summary: New premium lounges in Honolulu and Seattle will set a new standard of preflight comfort for guests traveling through the combined company’s two international hubs.
body_markdown:
## A premium lounge experience takes shape in Seattle


At Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, construction is underway on Alaska Airlines’


nearly


41,000-square-foot


l


ounge complex


located


in the


newly


expanded


C


Concourse


.


The space will bring two distinct experiences under one roof: a 500-seat Alaska Lounge and a 200-seat Aurora Lounge for Aurora Suites guests and eligible long-haul international travelers. The Aurora Lounge will be a key part of Alaska’s newly designed end-to-end guest experience unveiled last month to bring premium touches to every stage of the journey.


Scheduled to open in late 2027, the expansive


l


ounge


complex will be


the largest


lounge at SEA,


among the


biggest


in the United States and will further strengthen Seattle’s role as Alaska Air Group’s global gateway. Designed to


reflect


the spirit of the Pacific Northwest, it will offer guests a variety of ways to relax, work and dine before their journey. Highlights will include:


- Outdoor patio space with a fireplace


- Private work pods and wellness spaces


- Multiple premium bar experiences


- A coffee lab and fresh pastry offerings


- A pizza oven and locally inspired food and beverage program


- Premium shower suites and elevated dining experiences in the Aurora Lounge


Designed by Gensler and


being


built by PCL Construction, the new


SEA


l


ounge complex continues a partnership that has supported Alaska


L


ounge


projects in Seattle for more than a decade, including four


previous


builds and major renovations. This next chapter brings to life a destination designed around the evolving needs of domestic and international travelers.
